column1: # Intended divergences between the live verifier and frozen reference v1.
# ENUMERATED BY NAME, never by a threshold. The list is enforced in BOTH
# directions: a divergence that is not listed fails the suite, and a listed one
# that no longer occurs fails it too. A stale exception is a lie about the code,
# and it is the more dangerous of the two because it reads as coverage.
# Columns: <case-name> <direction> <reference-column> <reason — including the PR
# that approved it>
# DIRECTION is 수용→거부, 거부→수용, 수용→수용 or 거부→거부, as seen from
# reference v1 to the candidate. It is DERIVED from the two measured verdicts by
# the harness and the value written here is checked against that, so the label
# records understanding rather than granting permission.
# A 거부→수용 row is a LOSS OF DETECTION and cannot be listed without the
# literal marker DETECTION-LOSS in its reason. That marker is the only thing
# enforcing "detection does not get weaker"; without it a slice could enumerate
# its own regression and the list would rubber-stamp it.
# REFERENCE-COLUMN is 공통, A, B or C — which observable the frozen reference's
# `prev=` extractor produces for a row carrying an invalid byte on the leg where
# this row applies. The reference runs under a UTF-8 locale, because that is the
# locale production runs under, and the two implementations disagree there: BSD
# `sed` aborts and yields nothing (A), GNU `sed` returns a prefix it did not
# substitute (C). Both legs read this same file, so a row real on only one of
# them has to say which. The condition is checked in both directions — a row
# scoped to A that diverges under C fails as well, so the scope cannot be used
# as a quiet blanket.
# `강화 방향` declares whether this commit is one that tightens detection. When
# 예, the list must name at least one 수용→거부 case — a slice claiming to
# strengthen detection while producing no divergence at all has not been
# demonstrated to do anything. It is declared rather than inferred because which
# slice this is is a property of the commit, not of the tree.
# 강화 방향: 아니오
# Pinning the character-type axis neither strengthens nor weakens detection.
# Every row below is 거부→거부: the chain was already reported broken and still
# is, and what moved is WHICH ROW is named and WHY. Nothing that was accepted is
# now rejected, so 예 would be a claim this commit cannot support.
# WHY THE PIN IS SAFE, recorded here because this list is where the next reader
# arrives when they ask what the locale change was permitted to move.
# The pin is `LC_CTYPE=C`, scoped to four ledger readers by `local` + `export`:
# gate_chain_verify, gate_chain_tip, gate_ledger_damage and
# gate_pending_approvals_json.
# The argument that it cannot disturb the forced-surface digest is NOT "those
# functions contain no `sort`". That claim is checkable and it is FALSE —
# gate_pending_approvals_json, which this commit brings into scope, contains a
# `sort -u`. The argument that actually carries the weight is the separation of
# the two axes: sort order is decided by `LC_COLLATE`, and the driver exports
# `LC_COLLATE=C` unconditionally before any of this runs, so the collation axis
# is already pinned and this commit does not touch it. Measured — with
# `LC_COLLATE=C` held fixed, flipping `LC_CTYPE` between a UTF-8 locale and C
# leaves `sort -u` output byte-identical. The same separation covers the
# `[0-9a-f]` bracket expression in the `prev=` extractor, a range expression
# resolved on the collation axis too.

column4: 무효 바이트를 실은 행 1 에서 참조는 그 행을 지목한다 (BSD 는 sed 가 죽어 값이 비고, GNU 는 치환되지 않은 접두가 남아 어긋난다 — 경로는 다르나 지목 행은 같다). 고정된 추출자는 그 행의 prev= 를 올바로 읽어 내고 그 값은 맞으므로, 끊김은 실제로 어긋나는 다음 행에서 잡힌다. 지목이 한 행 뒤로 옮겨간 것이며 검출을 잃은 것이 아니다 (PR: 이 커밋)
